Suddenly, reverberating off the stone walls, a sound of thunder broke the silence. In the distance, we glimpsed immense beasts of the Mesozoic era roaming the dusty plains. The tyrannosaurus was stalking its prey, its head gleaming like a bronze statue. A few moments later, a blinding laser beam shot out of one of its eye sockets, isolating a lone brachiosaurus from the rest of the herd before cutting it in two. While the biomechanical menace chewed its freshly charred meal, we agreed that this environment would probably be a little too hostile to continue our experiments.

The words scatter and re-form as I move my pen across the page. Like rusty leaves transformed into beetles, they scurry off toward the margins. The ink gathers on the tip of my nib and goes back inside. The string binding the pages and the glue of the binding come undone and reconstitute themselves over and over again. All of it flutters through reality as if with a zoopraxiscope, the projection of images of timelines altered by minor changes.
